newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No deals yet for Russian firms to buy Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: No deals yet for Russian firms to buy Iraqi oil.

text.p: Russian companies, negotiating with Iraq to buy oil under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, will not be the first to get Iraqi oil, Russian traders and officials said on Monday.
"Russian firms are in talks, some representatives are in Baghdad, but as far as we know none of them has signed a formal deal," said an official with Russia's Alfa-Eko trading house.
"Western companies will be the first to start receiving Iraqi oil," he added. Alfa-Eko's officials will fly to Baghdad later this week, said the official who declined to be named.
Rosneft officials also said they knew of no further developments after the negotiations started. Nafta-Moskva declined to comment.

Market sources named Mashinoimport, Nafta-Moskva, Rosneft, Rosnefteimpex, MES (International Economic Coooperation), Alfa-Eko, AO Tatneft and OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil as those interested in buying Iraqi oil.

Iraqi oil will flow to world markets for the first time since United Nations sanctions were imposed on Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Friday he expected Iraqi oil exports to resume early on Tuesday.

Yuri Agababov, deputy director of oil and equipment supplier Zarubezhneft, said last week Russia could sign contracts for around 100,000 barrels a day but said it was too early to pin down figures. Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry had asked Zarubezhneft to act as coordinator.
